disclaimer: Wellness & Educational Forecasting Only — Not Medical Advice: This tool estimates behavioral fatigue patterns from self-logged habits and does not diagnose sleep disorders or medical conditions. Consult a qualified healthcare professional for persistent insomnia or exhaustion.

alerts.title: Caffeine Above Safe Daily Limit
alerts.detail: Average caffeine 480 mg/day is above the 400 mg/day ceiling for this context.

alerts.title: Suppressed Deep/REM Sleep Architecture
alerts.detail: Caffeine has a ~5 h half-life: about 169 mg is still active at bedtime on average, and 12 h of daily screen time delays melatonin. Deep (slow-wave) and REM sleep are reduced even when the clock total looks near 5.0 h.

alerts.title: Severe Cumulative Sleep Debt
alerts.detail: 21.0 h of unrepaid sleep debt against a 8.0 h baseline.

trajectory.label: Escalating
trajectory.note: Debt grew over the second half of the log. Unchanged habits point to a higher score next week.

formulas.name: 7-Day Sleep Debt
formulas.formula: gap = baseline − sleep. If gap > 0: debt += gap. Otherwise: debt = max(0, debt + 0.5 × gap). Surplus sleep repays only half as fast as a deficit builds. Start at debt = 0.

formulas.name: Caffeine Half-Life Residual
formulas.formula: residual = caffeine_mg × 0.5^(hours from last caffeine to bedtime ÷ 5). Upper-bound estimate: the whole day's caffeine is treated as taken at the last-caffeine time.

formulas.name: Circadian Midpoint Variance
formulas.formula: midpoint = bedtime + ((wake − bedtime) mod 24) ÷ 2. Midpoints are averaged on the 24 h circle; variance = RMS of each midpoint's circular deviation from that mean.

formulas.name: Architecture Efficiency
formulas.formula: 100 − min(30, 0.2 × mean residual) − min(15, 1.5 × max(0, mean screen − 4)) − min(15, 5 × midpoint SD) − min(20, 3 × max(0, baseline − mean sleep)), floor 20.

formulas.name: Weighted Burnout Composite Score
formulas.formula: 0.35·DebtScore + 0.15·CaffeineScore + 0.15·ScreenScore + 0.20·InconsistencyScore + 0.15·ArchitectureScore, then raised to the highest guardrail floor if one applies. DebtScore = min(100, debt ÷ 14 × 100); CaffeineScore = ½·min(100, max(0, mean caffeine ÷ limit − 0.5) × 100) + ½·min(100, mean residual ÷ reference × 100); ScreenScore = min(100, max(0, mean screen − 4) ÷ 8 × 100); InconsistencyScore = min(100, 0.6·(midpoint SD ÷ 2.5) × 100 + 0.4·(sleep SD ÷ 3) × 100); ArchitectureScore = min(100, (100 − efficiency) ÷ 50 × 100).

coach.headline: Critical burnout – urgent changes needed
coach.outlook: If you keep the same pattern, sleep debt will keep rising and you could hit 30 h of debt in a week. Caffeine will stay high, leaving ~170 mg in your system at bedtime, which will keep deep sleep suppressed. Your overall burnout score will likely stay in the critical range or worsen.

bottlenecks.title: Excess caffeine
bottlenecks.detail: Average 480 mg/day, 168 mg still in your body at bedtime, well above the 400 mg limit.

bottlenecks.title: Severe sleep debt
bottlenecks.detail: 21 h of cumulative debt; you’re averaging only 5 h of sleep versus an 8 h baseline.

bottlenecks.title: Long screen time
bottlenecks.detail: Almost 12 h of screens each day, pushing melatonin release later.

bottlenecks.title: Late bedtime
bottlenecks.detail: Bedtime around 01:30–02:00 while sleep anchor is 22:34, cutting sleep opportunity.

schedule.title: Wake up
schedule.detail: Get out of bed, open curtains for natural light.

schedule.title: Morning sunlight
schedule.detail: Spend 10 min outside or by a bright window to set your circadian clock.

schedule.title: Light movement
schedule.detail: Do a brief stretch or walk to boost alertness.

schedule.title: First caffeine
schedule.detail: Have a modest 100 mg coffee (no more than 1 cup).

schedule.title: Deep‑work window start
schedule.detail: Begin focused tasks; keep screens dim and use blue‑light filters.

schedule.title: Mid‑work movement break
schedule.detail: 5‑minute walk or stretch to reduce fatigue.

schedule.title: Deep‑work window end
schedule.detail: Wrap up high‑focus tasks before lunch.

schedule.title: Lunch & hydrate
schedule.detail: Balanced meal with protein, carbs, and vegetables; drink water.

schedule.title: Caffeine cutoff
schedule.detail: No more caffeine after this time; switch to water or herbal tea.

schedule.title: Afternoon light exposure
schedule.detail: Spend 10 min outside if possible to keep circadian rhythm steady.

schedule.title: Screen‑light break
schedule.detail: Turn off non‑essential screens for 30 min; use this time for a walk or reading.

schedule.title: Light dinner
schedule.detail: Eat a moderate meal, avoid heavy carbs late in the evening.

schedule.title: Evening wind‑down start
schedule.detail: Dim lights, stop work, begin relaxing activities.

schedule.title: Screen curfew
schedule.detail: All screens off; use amber filters if needed before digital sunset.

priorities: Cut daily caffeine to ≤400 mg and finish by 12:34 pm
Reduce screen time to ≤8 h/day and enforce a digital sunset at 21:04
Increase nightly sleep to at least 6.5 h by moving bedtime to 22:30‑23:00
